newsitem.title: GERMANY: Schrempp sticks to Daimler overhall plan - report.
newsitem.headline: Schrempp sticks to Daimler overhall plan - report.

text.p: Daimler-Benz AG chairman Juergen Schrempp is sticking to his plans for a massive reorganisation of the industrial group, a German magazine reported on Wednesday.

According to an article in the Stern magazine which will hit news-stands on Thursday, Schrempp said he is determined to make the group's car-and truck-making unit, Mercedes-Benz AG, part of the industrial group, ending its status as an independent company.
"It does not make sense to have several headquarters on top of one another," Schrempp was quoted as saying.
Stern said Schrempp expected the reorganisation to save the company about 400 million marks a year.

Daimler has been formulating a wide-ranging reorganisation plan for some months and hopes to make a final decision in January. Schrempp has said an overhaul is needed to speed decision-making and improve accountability among individual units.
Schrempp has faced opposition from within Daimler about the reorganisation, especially from Mercedes chairman Helmut Werner, who wants Mercedes to maintain its independence.

The Daimler chairman stressed that he hoped Werner would stay on after the reorganisation. According to some press reports, Werner has threatened to resign if Schrempp brought Mercedes closer within the group structure.
